items.title: 56799_Red Norvo oral history interview
items.q: Charlie Bollinger's band on the other side, which was a great band.

ctx.x: Right. And so they said, 'Well I don't know how we can get you with a band.' I said, this unless you're like a novelty thing. Novelty -- as far as the band's concerned.

And I said, 'Well I don't know what to say. What do you think I can do?' I said, 'Well I don't know.' But they liked what I did -- what I was trying to do. So they finally got me a job at Eagle's Ballroom in Milwaukee. IN front of the house band. Now we're playing -- there's two bands. There's a house band and Charlie Bollinger's band on the other side, which was a great band. A great band, swing band, jazz band. About 12-14 men. And we had a big band, so they made me director. And I stood out in front and I was…

So every -- during the evening, then I'd do a couple of specialties, and the people all call around and that's the way it started to work with bands. Now, finally this same office booked me in a place called Gull Lake, Michigan, with a band from Notre Dame. And I worked all summer and that was a great experience for me. Cause I really -- they had me in front of the band, now that band was organized, they had arrangements and they told me the tunes, and I learned the tunes and I played.
